classes.name: Veteran
classes.desc: They came home from the Argonne in 1919 and found work as extras, doormen and Legion boxers. Every one of them swore he was finished with fighting. Now the war has followed them to Hollywood Boulevard, so they dig in, hold the line and show the younger fellows how it's done.
spec_desc: The man who kept his squad alive in the Meuse-Argonne still does it, shield up and voice raised, standing wherever the mandibles land first.
Over the top with a two-handed weapon and no second thoughts. The bayonet charge worked in 1918, and the bugs have not read the field manuals.
Learned at the Legion smokers on Selma Avenue, a weapon in each fist and no bell to save anybody. Queensberry never wrote a rule for beetles.

classes.name: Stuntman
classes.desc: They fell off horses, trains and the roofs of Poverty Row for seven-fifty a day and a bandage. When the bugs took the lots, the men who doubled for the stars found the real fight paid no better and hurt about the same. They hit first and land on their feet.
spec_desc: Saloon brawls were staged with pulled punches. Out here nobody pulls anything, and a man who can throw one for the camera learns fast to throw one for keeps.
Prop knives were rubber. The ones in a stuntman's boot these days are Sheffield steel, honed nightly and slipped between chitin plates where the hive forgot to armour.
The trick to a forty-foot fall is knowing where the boxes are. The trick with an insect's charge is the same: be somewhere else, and land laughing.

classes.name: Gunman
classes.desc: Trick shooters from the Wild West shows, Gower Gulch cowboys, game wardens and the men who loaded blanks at Stembridge on Marathon Street. When the bugs came, somebody swapped the blanks for live rounds. Gunmen keep their distance, keep their heads and keep count of the shells.
spec_desc: One rifle, one rest, one breath held. Marksmen learned the trade in the Argonne or on the deer runs above Tujunga, and they do not waste a cartridge.
Annie Oakley's heirs, late of the Miller Brothers 101 Ranch show: shooting from the hip, off the mirror, with both hands at once. The bugs never applaud.
Hound men from the canyons and the studio animal pens, working a dog that has learned what a hive smells like. The dog finds them; the gun finishes it.

classes.name: Electrician
classes.desc: The juicers who ran cable and trimmed carbon arcs on every sound stage in town. When the hive took the lots, they kept the keys to the powerhouse and learned that a thousand amps cooks a beetle as well as it lights a starlet. Union men, mostly, and still sore about the overtime.
spec_desc: Strike the arc and hold it on one target. The blue-white spark that burns down a carbon rod burns through chitin just as easily, and it does not wander.
A ten-thousand-watt sun on wheels, swung across a whole swarm at once. Things raised in the dark of a hive hate a key light worse than poison.
Portable dynamos hauled off the location trucks and wound to throw a crackling skin of current around the crew. Anything that bites through it gets a mouthful.

classes.name: Powder Man
classes.desc: Studio effects men who blew up Atlanta twice a week and swept up the cork by supper. They know black powder, flash paper and smoke pots better than their own children. When the hive took the lots, they took the powder magazine with them.
spec_desc: Gasoline, magnesium and a steady match. A Fire man sets the blaze, stands back and lets it eat slow, the way it ate the Babylon set.
Smoke pots made a thousand battlefields on a ten-dollar budget. Now they blind compound eyes, choke the drones and hide a man who needs to be elsewhere.
The big charges, wired by hand and touched off from behind a sandbag. Demolition men measure success by how far the windows rattled on Vine.

classes.name: Nurse
classes.desc: They came from Hollywood Hospital, the studio first-aid huts and the base hospitals of France, and they have seen worse than bugs. Now they work double shifts in the Roosevelt lobby and the gutters of Highland Avenue. Nobody on the line argues with a nurse twice.
spec_desc: Tag the dying, patch the living, move to the next cot. Triage nurses learned it in France, where the stretchers never stopped coming and neither did they.
Slow work and sure: carbolic, clean dressings, a spoonful of something bitter on the hour. A good nurse keeps a man mending long after she has left his bedside.
Every hospital dispensary holds enough to kill a horse, and most bugs are smaller than a horse. The nurse measures carefully, then pours generously.

classes.name: Preacher
classes.desc: Tent revivalists, storefront pastors and Angelus Temple choir hands who were saving Hollywood's soul long before anything landed on it. They carry a cane, a worn Bible and a voice that fills five thousand seats. Now they patch up sinners and saints alike, and preach fire at anything with six legs.
spec_desc: Hymns sung loud enough to carry over gunfire. When the whole congregation is bleeding, the Gospel preacher lifts every voice in the room back onto its feet.
The dry crusade turned to armour. Temperance preachers stand between the faithful and harm the way they once stood between a thirsty man and his bottle.
Sawdust-trail sermons with the brimstone left in. The Hellfire preacher calls down judgment on the hive, and the hive, for once, listens.

classes.name: Mechanic
classes.desc: Garage men, studio grips and camera-truck mechanics who kept the lots running on baling wire and bad language. Since the Dome came down they fix what the bugs break, rig what the bugs fear, and swing a sledge at whatever won't stay fixed.
spec_desc: Tin-can alarms, spring traps and a motor-driven contraption that spits rivets. If it ticks, whirs or goes off when nobody expected it, a Gadgets man built it in a garage.
A four-pound sledge, a tire iron, a pipe wrench as long as a man's arm. The insects grow hard shells; the Heavy Tools men bring harder answers.
Splints, tourniquets and a canvas kit of patches that work on people about as well as on radiators. Nobody asks where the rubber hose came from.

abilities.name: Bayonet Thrust
abilities.desc: A hard thrust: weapon damage plus 6.
abilities.flavor: The same short, ugly lunge they drilled at Camp Kearny, twelve years on. The steel goes in where the shell plates part.

abilities.name: Sergeant's Bark
abilities.desc: Gain 20 Adrenaline and deal 10% more damage for 20 s.
abilities.flavor: A voice built for artillery and parade grounds. Men stand straighter, and somewhere a bug three blocks off stops chewing.

abilities.name: Hold the Line
abilities.desc: Force the target to attack you for 4 s. High threat.
abilities.flavor: You plant your boots and make yourself the biggest, loudest, most insulting thing on the street. The bug takes the bait.

abilities.name: Trench Sweep
abilities.desc: Strike every enemy within 6 m of your target.
abilities.flavor: A wide, flat swing learned in a crowded trench, where the enemy came in threes and nobody had room to be polite.

abilities.name: Rifle Butt
abilities.flavor: The Army never wrote it in the manual, but every doughboy knew the wooden end works fine too.

abilities.name: Dig In
abilities.flavor: Shoulders down, chin tucked, feet in the dirt like the Argonne all over again. Let it come.

abilities.name: Over the Top
abilities.desc: A finishing blow: 160% weapon damage plus 14.
abilities.flavor: The whistle blows in your head and you go, the way you went in 1918, and this time you mean to finish it.

abilities.name: Haymaker
abilities.desc: A wild swing: weapon damage plus 6.
abilities.flavor: Thrown from the hip like the cowboy who started every saloon brawl on the Columbia lot. Wild, wide and telegraphed from Pasadena, and it lands anyway.

abilities.name: Tumble
abilities.flavor: A shoulder roll learned on a thousand takes. The mandible snaps shut on the spot where you stood a moment ago.

abilities.name: Low Blow
abilities.flavor: The Production Code forbids it on screen. Nobody under the Dome is filming, and the thing folds up just the same.

abilities.name: Knife Flurry
abilities.desc: Three fast cuts: 170% weapon damage plus 8.
abilities.flavor: Three cuts faster than a newsreel can follow, the kind of work the studios hired you to fake and never knew you could do for real.

abilities.name: Breakaway Bottle
abilities.desc: Throw a bottle: damage and a 50% slow for 6 s.
abilities.flavor: Sugar glass from the prop room, made to shatter harmlessly over a leading man. Nobody told the prop man what gets poured inside it now.

abilities.name: Death-Defying Leap
abilities.desc: Hit every enemy within 6 m of you.
abilities.flavor: The same jump that took you off a Gower Street rooftop for two dollars a fall. You come down boots first on everything around you.

abilities.name: Showstopper
abilities.flavor: The finish you saved for the picture that never got made. Somewhere a director would have shouted cut and printed it.

abilities.name: Aimed Shot
abilities.desc: A careful shot: 150% weapon damage plus 8.
abilities.flavor: Breathe out, lay the bead on the joint behind the head, squeeze. The shot that wins the turkey at the county fair, here spent on something with six legs.

abilities.name: Hip Fire
abilities.flavor: No sighting, no ceremony. The gun clears leather and speaks before the bug has finished turning around.

abilities.name: Knee Shot
abilities.desc: Slow the target by 50% for 6 s.
abilities.flavor: A round into the leg joint where the shell is thinnest. Even a hive soldier limps when it has one less knee to stand on.

abilities.name: Fan the Hammer
abilities.desc: Empty the cylinder: 200% weapon damage plus 10.
abilities.flavor: Palm slapping the hammer, six shots so close together the extras on Gower Street would swear it was one long one.

abilities.name: Buckshot
abilities.desc: Hit every enemy within 6 m of the target.
abilities.flavor: A shell of double-ought sprays the whole knot of them. The bugs bunch up like a crowd at a premiere, and pay for it.

abilities.name: Steady Nerves
abilities.flavor: The hands stop shaking, the noise goes far away, and every shell joint on the field looks big as a barn door.

abilities.name: Dead to Rights
abilities.flavor: The bug is caught square, nowhere to run, and the gunman takes his time. Some shots end the argument outright.

abilities.name: Arc
abilities.flavor: A blue spark leaps from the wrench tip with a crack like a slapstick. The bug twitches, and the air smells of a stage after a thunderstorm scene.

abilities.name: Insulate
abilities.desc: A shield that absorbs damage for 20 s.
abilities.flavor: Rubber, mica and a prayer, wound round the body the way you'd tape a cable. Claws skid off it like rain off a studio umbrella.

abilities.name: Live Wire
abilities.desc: Shocks the target every 3 s for 12 s.
abilities.flavor: A loose cable lashes onto the target and stays there, spitting sparks on a steady count. It hums like a neon sign on Vine.

abilities.name: Floodlight
abilities.desc: Burn every enemy within 8 m of the target.
abilities.flavor: A ten-thousand-watt studio lamp swings round and opens up. Anything caught in the beam cooks like a starlet under the old carbon arcs.

abilities.name: Short Circuit
abilities.flavor: One bad splice, done on purpose. The bug locks rigid with its feelers standing straight up, like an extra who's forgotten his line.

abilities.name: Overload
abilities.flavor: Every breaker on the board thrown at once, the lamp bulbs popping down the line. It takes a moment to build, and the bug never forgets it.

abilities.name: Chain Lightning
abilities.desc: Lightning jumps between enemies within 10 m of the target.
abilities.flavor: The current isn't fussy about who it meets. It jumps from shell to shell down the line like gossip through the Brown Derby.

abilities.name: Flash Powder
abilities.flavor: A pinch of magnesium in the tray, a thumb on the trigger, and a white bang that would make any newsreel cameraman reach for his hat.

abilities.name: Slow Fuse
abilities.desc: The target burns every 3 s for 15 s.
abilities.flavor: The powder man lights it and walks away. The bug never hears the hiss until its shell starts to blister from the inside.

abilities.name: Smoke Pot
abilities.desc: Slow every enemy within 8 m of the target by 50% for 8 s.
abilities.flavor: A tin pot from the effects truck, good for battlefield scenes and burning barns. Insects lose their way in it as badly as extras do.

abilities.name: Squib
abilities.flavor: The little charge they tape under a shirt to make a gunshot look real. Taped to a carapace, it does not need to look like anything.

abilities.name: Powder Keg
abilities.desc: Blast every enemy within 8 m of the target.
abilities.flavor: Black powder, a stout oak keg and a short fuse. In the war they'd have called it excessive; on a studio lot they call it Tuesday.

abilities.name: Smokescreen
abilities.flavor: He cracks a canister at his own feet and steps sideways into the grey. Claws close on smoke and come away empty.

abilities.name: Demolition Charge
abilities.flavor: The charge they save for blowing up a whole set in one take. Studio insurance men would weep; there are none left to ask.

abilities.name: Ether Rag
abilities.flavor: A rag soaked from the brown bottle, pressed hard over whatever passes for a face. The fumes do the rest, and the nurse holds her breath.

abilities.name: Dress Wound
abilities.flavor: Clean gauze, a firm hand and a safety pin. She has wrapped worse on extras who fell off horses in Gower Gulch.

abilities.name: Tonic
abilities.flavor: A spoonful of something bitter from an unlabelled bottle. It warms the chest slowly and keeps on working long after the face stops puckering.

abilities.name: Smelling Salts
abilities.flavor: One sharp whiff under the nose and the fallen sit bolt upright, eyes watering, asking who hit them.

abilities.name: Iodine Splash
abilities.flavor: A flung bottle of iodine splashes brown across the carapace and keeps burning. It stings people too, as every child in Los Angeles can tell you.

abilities.name: Field Surgery
abilities.flavor: Sleeves up, lamp held close, forceps and catgut on a folding table. Not a hospital, but the patient lives to complain about it.

abilities.name: Sedative
abilities.flavor: A syringe driven in at the soft joint between plates. Even a hive soldier stops to think about that, then stops thinking altogether.

abilities.name: Rebuke
abilities.flavor: A finger leveled and a verse from Ezekiel, delivered like a slap. The insect reels as if someone had struck it with the Book itself.

abilities.name: Lay On Hands
abilities.flavor: Two calloused palms on a bloody shoulder, eyes shut, lips moving. The bleeding slows, the breathing steadies, and nobody asks how.

abilities.name: Blessing
abilities.desc: A shield that absorbs damage for 20 s.
abilities.flavor: A quick sign of the cross and a word over the head. Claws come down and glance off something nobody can see.

abilities.name: Hellfire Sermon
abilities.flavor: Brimstone, delivered at full volume in the Angelus Temple style. The words catch on the target like a lit fuse and keep burning.

abilities.name: Hymn
abilities.desc: Heal every party member within 30 m.
abilities.flavor: An old Methodist tune, sung loud enough to carry over gunfire. Everyone within earshot stands a little straighter and bleeds a little less.

abilities.name: Fear of God
abilities.flavor: The preacher draws himself up and roars Judgment. Even a four-metre hive brute freezes, unsure what just happened to it.

abilities.name: Revival
abilities.flavor: The tent-meeting cure, full fervour and both arms raised. Men who were halfway to Hollywood Cemetery get up and ask for their hats.

abilities.name: Wrench Swing
abilities.flavor: Fourteen inches of drop-forged steel, swung like a man who has stripped a thousand rusted nuts and finally found something that deserves it.

abilities.name: Patch Kit
abilities.flavor: Friction tape, a dab of axle grease and a clean rag from the back pocket. It held a Model A together; it will hold you.

abilities.name: Caltrops
abilities.desc: Slow every enemy within 8 m by 50% for 8 s.
abilities.flavor: A coffee can of roofing nails and bent bolts flung across the pavement. Six legs or two, nobody crosses that without picking their way.

abilities.name: Monkey Wrench
abilities.flavor: Thrown end over end at the head. Somewhere on the lot a foreman is still asking who walked off with his good wrench.

abilities.name: Arc Welder
abilities.desc: Burn every enemy within 5 m of the target.
abilities.flavor: The torch spits blue-white fire and molten bead. Studio welders learned to work without goggles the day the bugs came over the wall.

abilities.name: Overhaul
abilities.desc: Heal yourself and gain 50% armour for 15 s.
abilities.flavor: Tighten every buckle, hammer the dents flat, bolt a sheet of boiler plate over the bad spot. Ugly work, but it runs.

abilities.name: Pile Driver
abilities.flavor: Both hands, full weight, straight down, the way the gangs drove piling for the Mulholland Dam. Shells crack the same as timber.

abilities.name: Acid Spit
abilities.desc: Acid: a hit, then 3 x 20% of a hit over 6 s.

abilities.name: Acid Pool
abilities.desc: Acid splashes everyone near the target.

talents.name: Parade Ground
talents.desc: Twelve years on, the knees still lock and the chin still lifts when a sergeant's voice carries. The bugs have yet to see you slouch.

talents.name: Barked Orders
talents.desc: You learned to make yourself heard over a barrage at Saint-Mihiel. A few insects clicking in a soundstage are no competition.

talents.name: Sandbagged
talents.desc: You stand behind your shield the way you stood behind a sandbag wall in the Argonne: low, square and in no hurry to leave.

talents.name: Hold Fast
talents.desc: Plant the boots, square the shoulders and let the whole hive come to you. They usually do, and they usually regret it.

talents.name: Bayonet Drill
talents.desc: Long point, short point, withdraw. The straw dummies at Camp Kearny never fought back, but the lesson took all the same.

talents.name: Marching Order
talents.desc: Sixty pounds of pack up a Vosges hill builds a man's back. Hollywood's hills are kinder, and the load is mostly ammunition now.

talents.name: No Man's Land
talents.desc: Nobody who crossed the wire comes home wasting a swing. You find the soft joint in the chitin the way you found the gap in the barbed wire.

talents.name: The Whistle Blows
talents.desc: A tin whistle, a lungful of air, and every man goes up the ladder at once. Some habits a fellow never puts in the attic.

talents.name: Bar-Room Manners
talents.desc: Learned in the back rooms of Gower Street speakeasies: hit first, hit low, and never let the other fellow finish his sentence.

talents.name: Thick Skull
talents.desc: The doctors at Letterman said the shrapnel should have killed you. Your mother said you were always too stubborn to listen.

talents.name: Rifle-Butt Habit
talents.desc: When the magazine's empty and the bug's too close, the wrong end of a Springfield works just as well. Better, some say.

talents.name: Sawdust Footwork
talents.desc: The Legion stadium on El Centro teaches you to slip a punch on sawdust. A pincer comes slower than a middleweight's left.

talents.name: Roadwork
talents.desc: Five miles before breakfast, up Vine and back, in a sweatshirt and borrowed boots. The fellows at the Legion stadium swear by it, and so do their lungs.

talents.name: Telegraphed Haymaker
talents.desc: Every extra in Gower Gulch can see it coming from across the lot. The trick is that seeing it coming doesn't help one bit.

talents.name: No Glass Jaw
talents.desc: Ten years of taking stage punches that landed for real. The jaw is set like poured concrete now, and the dentist sends a card at Christmas.

talents.name: Dirty Pool
talents.desc: The Marquess of Queensberry never fought a four-metre beetle. A knee where it counts, a thumb in the eye, and back for more.

talents.name: Sharp Edges
talents.desc: A whetstone in the hip pocket and a habit of using it between takes. The blade finds the seams in the shell like it knows the way.

talents.name: Quick Hands
talents.desc: Card tricks at the commissary, coin rolls on set, a knife where nobody saw one a moment ago. The hands move before the eyes catch up.

talents.name: Second Unit Flurry
talents.desc: The second unit shoots the fights the stars won't do, fast and cheap and all in one go. Nobody counts the cuts, least of all the bug.

talents.name: Props Department
talents.desc: Prop bottles are sugar glass. These are not. The props man looks the other way, and Prohibition makes sure the bottles are already empty.

talents.name: Tuck and Roll
talents.desc: Hit the ground shoulder first, chin tucked, and come up running. Every stuntman learns it on the mat, or learns it in the hospital.

talents.name: Cable Work
talents.desc: Months on piano wire and pulleys teach a body to move light and quick. The rigging is gone, but the feet still remember it.

talents.name: High Fall
talents.desc: Off the top of a set, through the awning, onto whatever waits below. The cardboard boxes are optional; landing on something with legs is better.

talents.name: One Take
talents.desc: Film stock costs money, and so does a second try. Get it right the first time, then get up and do it again.

talents.name: Steady Hand
talents.desc: Breath out slow, squeeze, don't pull. The rifle sits still as a tripod while the bug crosses the sights.

talents.name: Long Sight
talents.desc: Years of watching ridgelines teach the eye to catch a feeler twitching three blocks off, past the billboards.

talents.name: Dead Eye
talents.desc: Some men hit the bug. You hit the soft joint between the plates, every time, like threading a needle.

talents.name: Dead to Rights
talents.desc: The bug has nowhere left to go, and it knows. You finish the sentence the way a judge would.

talents.name: Fast Draw
talents.desc: Learned from the Gower Gulch cowboys, who practised it between takes for a dollar a day and lunch. The iron clears leather before the mandibles open.

talents.name: Show-Off
talents.desc: A little flourish never hurt anybody, except the bug. The extras on the sidewalk still clap.

talents.name: Fanning
talents.desc: Palm slapping the hammer, six shots in a heartbeat. Tom Mix did it for the camera; you do it for keeps.

talents.name: Cool Head
talents.desc: The bug screams, the street burns, and you are thinking about where you left your hat. Nerves like that pay for themselves.

talents.name: Tracker
talents.desc: Broken chaparral, a smear of ichor on a fence post. You follow the trail at a hunter's lope through Griffith Park brush.

talents.name: Camp Life
talents.desc: Cold beans, a bedroll under a pepper tree and the dog for a pillow. Nights in Vermont Canyon toughen a body up.

talents.name: Hamstring Shot
talents.desc: Aim low for the leg joint. A bug that can't run is a bug that waits politely for the second shot.

talents.name: Heavy Buckshot
talents.desc: Hand-loaded shells packed heavier than Stembridge would ever rent out. The kick bruises a shoulder and empties a doorway.

talents.name: High Tension
talents.desc: Run the line hot enough and the arc jumps before you ask it to. The wire hums like a hornet shut in a mason jar.

talents.name: Bare Copper
talents.desc: Strip the insulation and the current bites harder. The union safety man would have words, but he's in a cocoon on Stage 4.

talents.name: Hot Line
talents.desc: A live cable whipped across a soundstage floor finds whatever is standing on it. Bugs, as a rule, stand on a great many legs.

talents.name: Forked Path
talents.desc: Lightning never cared for one road. Yours leaps from shell to shell down the line, quick as gossip at the Brown Derby.

talents.name: Carbon Arc
talents.desc: The carbon rods burn white as a July noon. Sun arcs lit the dogfights in Hell's Angels; now they light anything with antennae.

talents.name: Key Light
talents.desc: The cameraman's first rule: set your key light and everything else falls into place. Think the shot through before you throw the switch.

talents.name: Spill Light
talents.desc: Light never stays where the gaffer puts it. Neither does the harm, and nobody on the receiving end files a complaint.

talents.name: Blackout
talents.desc: Pull the main breaker and a whole stage goes dark. Practice makes the trip quicker, and the bugs never get used to it.

talents.name: Dynamo
talents.desc: A man who works beside a running dynamo learns to take a jolt and keep his feet. The hum gets into his bones.

talents.name: Grounded
talents.desc: Every good rig has its ground wire. Run one through your own coat and the worst of it drains harmlessly into the floor.

talents.name: Flywheel
talents.desc: Once a flywheel spins up, it keeps turning long after the motor quits. A good electrician finds his second wind the same way.

talents.name: Fuse Box
talents.desc: Anyone can blow a fuse. It takes a studio electrician to blow one on purpose, on the cheap, and exactly where the bug is standing.

talents.name: Magnesium
talents.desc: A pinch more magnesium in the flash tray. The bugs see white for a long second, and so does anyone who forgot to look away.

talents.name: Long Fuse
talents.desc: Cut the fuse long and let it hiss. A patient man gets more out of every inch of powder.

talents.name: Slow Burn
talents.desc: Some fires flare and die. Yours settle in like a boarder who pays on time and never leaves.

talents.name: Squib Rig
talents.desc: The same little charges that burst blood packs on Western sets, wired tighter and packed meaner. Nobody yells cut.

talents.name: Lampblack
talents.desc: A smear of soot across the face and coat. In a smoky room, a man the colour of smoke is hard to hit.

talents.name: Fog Machine
talents.desc: The studio fog rig, mended with baling wire and a prayer. It coughs up a fresh bank sooner than it ought to.

talents.name: Under Cover
talents.desc: Stay low, stay in the haze, and let the claws find the drifting smoke instead of you.

talents.name: Thick Smokescreen
talents.desc: Navy men taught it on destroyers in the war. A screen that thick hides a retreat or a whole ambush.

talents.name: Black Powder
talents.desc: Good old-fashioned black powder, the kind grandfather used on tree stumps. Coarse, honest and loud.

talents.name: Steady Fingers
talents.desc: Hands that never shook through Mack Sennett's worst stunts. A steady hand makes a clever head.

talents.name: Bigger Keg
talents.desc: The prop department said the keg was too big. The prop department is not out here fighting bugs.

talents.name: Shaped Charge
talents.desc: Pack it in a cone, point it right, and the whole blast goes where you send it. Mining men swear by it.

talents.name: Quick Dressing
talents.desc: Gauze goes on in three turns and a knot, before the man has finished swearing. The Army taught it; the Boulevard perfected it.

talents.name: Night Shift
talents.desc: The lamps on Hollywood Boulevard go dark at ten. The aid station does not, and neither does she, beside a pot of coffee long gone cold.

talents.name: Triage
talents.desc: Three men on the pavement and one pair of hands. She looks once at each and knows who can wait.

talents.name: Strong Salts
talents.desc: One whiff of ammonia and a fainted extra sits bolt upright, ready to fight a beetle the size of a Ford.

talents.name: Patent Tonic
talents.desc: Nobody reads the label too closely, which is a mercy under the Volstead Act. It warms the blood all the same.

talents.name: Bedside Manner
talents.desc: A calm voice, a cool hand, and a promise that the doctor is on his way. Nobody has seen the doctor since August.

talents.name: Steady Scalpel
talents.desc: Under a flickering lamp, with the hive humming through the walls, the blade does not waver by a hair.

talents.name: Rationing
talents.desc: Half a roll of gauze, a quarter-bottle of carbolic, a pencil tally on the cupboard door. Nothing under the Dome is wasted twice.

talents.name: Tincture of Iodine
talents.desc: It stings a man and blisters a bug. The brown stains on her cuffs tell you which she's been treating lately.

talents.name: Ether Fumes
talents.desc: A soaked pad, a sweet heavy smell, and something with far too many legs forgets what it was doing.

talents.name: Lab Coat
talents.desc: Starched cotton, stained with things that ought not to exist. It turns acid and spit better than you would think.

talents.name: Double Dose
talents.desc: The label says one spoonful. The label was written for people, not for a hornet as long as a delivery truck.

talents.name: Laying On
talents.desc: The preacher's palms press flat on a fevered brow and stay there, firm as a notary's stamp, until the shaking stops.

talents.name: Tent Revival
talents.desc: Sawdust floor, canvas walls, a hundred folding chairs and one voice that will not quit before midnight. The spirit catches like dry brush.

talents.name: Hymnal
talents.desc: The old hymns come easier now, every verse by heart, and the wounded find themselves humming along between gasps.

talents.name: Collection Plate
talents.desc: Pass the plate and folks give what they can: a nickel, a button, a moment's rest. It all adds up by Sunday.

talents.name: Teetotal
talents.desc: Not a drop since Coolidge. The liver is pristine, the knees are sturdy, and the bootleggers on Vine cross the street to avoid the sermon.

talents.name: Abiding Blessing
talents.desc: The blessing settles on a shoulder like a good wool coat and stays put, long after the amen.

talents.name: Dry County
talents.desc: No liquor, no excuses, no soft spots. A body kept dry and plain takes a blow the way a church door takes a storm.

talents.name: The Pledge
talents.desc: Sign the temperance pledge and the Lord keeps His end promptly. The blessing comes round again before the ink is dry.

talents.name: Brimstone
talents.desc: The sermon smells of sulphur now. Insects in the front pews start to smoke at the joints before the second point.

talents.name: Sharp Rebuke
talents.desc: A word from the pulpit, sharp as a ruler across the knuckles. Even a hive drone flinches at being told off properly.

talents.name: Righteous Wrath
talents.desc: Some days the Lord is patient. Other days He lends the preacher a cane and a very good aim.

talents.name: Fire and Brimstone
talents.desc: Damnation described in such loving detail that beetles the size of Packards turn tail and scuttle for the hills.

talents.name: Tinkerer
talents.desc: Every alarm clock on the Boulevard has been opened up on a kitchen table at least once. You just never stopped asking how things work.

talents.name: Roofing Nails
talents.desc: A keg of roofing nails from a Gower Street lumberyard, scattered wide. Six legs feel every one of them.

talents.name: Hotter Torch
talents.desc: Open the acetylene valve another quarter turn. The flame goes from orange to a hissing blue that cuts chitin like tin.

talents.name: Spare Parts
talents.desc: Coat pockets full of washers, cotter pins and a carburettor float nobody asked about. Something always fits.

talents.name: Torque
talents.desc: It's not the size of the wrench, it's the shoulders behind it. Put your back into the swing and the bolt gives.

talents.name: Shop Floor
talents.desc: Ten years hauling engine blocks across a Burbank garage floor builds the kind of arms that don't need a hoist.

talents.name: Heavy Iron
talents.desc: Forged steel, no aluminium nonsense. When it lands, the bug knows it was hit by something made in Pittsburgh.

talents.name: Steam Hammer
talents.desc: Borrowed from a pier crew in San Pedro, near enough. Each blow lands like a piling going into bedrock, and comes back around sooner.

talents.name: Coveralls
talents.desc: Heavy denim, double-stitched, stiff with a decade of motor oil. Mandibles slide right off the grime.

talents.name: Bigger Patches
talents.desc: Why use a strip of rubber when you can use the whole inner tube? A wider patch holds a fellow together longer.

talents.name: Full Overhaul
talents.desc: Strip it down, clean it, put it back together better than the factory did. Works on Fords and on people, mostly.

talents.name: Grease Monkey
talents.desc: They called you a grease monkey at the Packard dealership. Now the grease is the only reason you're still standing.

talents.name: Mess Hall Rations
talents.desc: Bully beef, hardtack and coffee you could stand a spoon in. Nobody liked it, but it kept a man on his feet till Tuesday.

talents.name: Kitchener's Stare
talents.desc: The old recruiting-poster glare, pointing finger and all. A Veteran holds the line now without spending half his breath shouting about it.

talents.name: Duckboard Footing
talents.desc: Months on slatted boards over Flanders mud taught him where his feet go. A shield set on firm footing does not give.

talents.name: Dugout Discipline
talents.desc: He learned to go to ground fast when the whistle blew. Sandbags, shovel, head down, all before the second shell lands.

talents.name: Second Wind
talents.desc: Halfway up Vine with a bug the size of a Packard behind him, something old and stubborn kicks in. The breath comes back.

talents.name: Spit and Polish
talents.desc: Boots blacked, buttons bright, helmet strap mended. A man who keeps his kit in order finds the claws skid off it more often.

talents.name: Drill Sergeant
talents.desc: A voice that once cleared a parade ground at Camp Kearny. The bugs turn toward it the way the recruits used to.

talents.name: Dry Socks
talents.desc: Every veteran remembers trench foot. Fresh wool socks mean quick feet, and quick feet mean the stinger hits pavement instead.

talents.name: Rum Ration
talents.desc: Prohibition says no. The Sergeant says a tot before the push never hurt anybody, and he keeps a flask to prove it.

talents.name: Kit Inspection
talents.desc: Bayonet oiled, entrenching tool sharpened, nothing rattling. A clean kit swings easier and wastes less of the man carrying it.

talents.name: The Last Ditch
talents.desc: There is always one more trench behind you, until there isn't. In that last one, a Veteran stops being a man and becomes a wall.

talents.name: Stripes Earned
talents.desc: Not handed out at Central Casting. Sewn on in France, for men who carried more than their share and brought others home.

talents.name: Fixed Bayonets
talents.desc: The click of a bayonet locking home on the lug. After that, every lunge comes cheap and comes without a second thought.

talents.name: Creeping Barrage
talents.desc: Walk the fire forward and walk in behind it. His swings roll across a swarm like shellbursts across no man's land.

talents.name: Lee-Enfield Weight
talents.desc: Nine pounds of rifle changes a man's idea of a blow. He swings everything now as if it had a brass butt plate.

talents.name: Trench Raider
talents.desc: Night raids taught quick work in close quarters: in, swing, out before the flares go up. The habit never left him.

talents.name: Short Rush
talents.desc: Up, run, down, five seconds and never more, the sergeants said. A Veteran still crosses Highland Avenue that way.

talents.name: Blood Up
talents.desc: The fight gets into him like a fever. The harder the bugs push, the hotter and steadier he burns.

talents.name: Light Pack
talents.desc: Leave the greatcoat, the spare boots and the letters home. Going over the top costs less when you're not hauling a mule's load.

talents.name: Kill or Be Killed
talents.desc: The bayonet instructor's only lesson, shouted till it stuck. Twelve years on, the reflexes still answer before the Veteran thinks.

talents.name: Iron Nerve
talents.desc: Shells came down at Belleau Wood and he kept digging. A bug the size of a Ford is just one more thing that won't hurry him.

talents.name: Hard Tack
talents.desc: Army biscuit hard enough to drive nails. Men who lived on it in France find a hive siege no great hardship on the stomach.

talents.name: Over and Out
talents.desc: Over the top and out the other side. The whistle blows, the line goes forward, and whatever waits in the wire gets the bayonet.

talents.name: Shell-Shocked Calm
talents.desc: Some men came home shaking. Some came home very, very still. The stillness keeps a fellow on his feet long after sense says lie down.

talents.name: Cauliflower Ear
talents.desc: Years of Legion smokers at El Centro and Selma taught him to roll with a punch, whether it comes from a heavyweight or a mandible.

talents.name: Saloon Shove
talents.desc: No need to wind up for it. A short jab with the rifle butt, same as clearing the bar rail on payday.

talents.name: Prohibition Gin
talents.desc: A medicinal pint from a friendly druggist. It tastes like turpentine and puts colour back in a man's face faster than it has any right to.

talents.name: Knuckle-Duster
talents.desc: Brass knuckles on the off hand put weight behind every thrust. The Marquis of Queensberry never wrote rules for anything with six legs.

talents.name: The Clinch
talents.desc: Tie up the arms, lean in, smother the punches. It works on a southpaw from San Pedro and, it turns out, on a mantis.

talents.name: Rough House
talents.desc: He kicks over tables, insults their mothers and makes himself the loudest thing in the room. The bugs take it personally.

talents.name: Stunt Double
talents.desc: Padding borrowed from the stunt department, sewn under the tunic. Built to take a fall from a stagecoach, it takes a claw nearly as well.

talents.name: Back-Lot Scrapper
talents.desc: Learned between the false fronts on the backlot, where extras settled their quarrels. Fight short, fight dirty, and find the soft spot first.

talents.name: Speakeasy Bouncer
talents.desc: Clearing a crowded speakeasy at closing time takes one broad swing and no apologies. The hive gets the same courtesy.

talents.name: Studio Muscle
talents.desc: The studios paid good money for big men to stand at the gate and look discouraging. He has the build and has kept it.

talents.name: Last Man Standing
talents.desc: When the line breaks and the others go down, something old and stubborn wakes in him. Nothing lands clean after that.

talents.name: Pug's Grin
talents.desc: Missing teeth, a flattened nose and a smile that says he has tasted worse than whatever the hive is spitting.

talents.name: Studio Gym
talents.desc: Mornings on the pulley weights in the lot gym, between calls. The muscle a picture needs, built where the extras eat their lunch.

talents.name: Cauliflower Ear
talents.desc: Every fall and fistfight leaves something behind. Yours is an ear like a boiled cabbage and a body that has stopped taking hits personally.

talents.name: Pulled Punch
talents.desc: Studio fighters learn a punch that misses by an inch on camera. Out here you throw the same tidy swing, minus the wasted wind-up.

talents.name: Main Event
talents.desc: You fight like the last reel, when the whole house is on its feet and the organist leans on every key at once.

talents.name: Two-Reel Brawler
talents.desc: Two reels, twenty minutes, a saloon fight in each. You learned to keep swinging long after the comedian would have taken his pie and gone home.

talents.name: Bum's Rush
talents.desc: Grab a collar, grab a belt, and run them out the door. The bouncers at the Brown Derby never did it quicker.

talents.name: Stand-Up Guy
talents.desc: You don't back down and you don't go down. Forearms come up, the blow slides off, and you're still standing there waiting.

talents.name: Below the Belt
talents.desc: The Marquess of Queensberry never fought anything with six legs. A knee where it counts costs you nothing but your good name.

talents.name: Sucker Punch
talents.desc: Wait until they look at somebody else. The best punch in any picture is the one the heavy never saw coming.

talents.name: Iron Chin
talents.desc: The studio doctor gave up X-raying your jaw years ago. Whatever comes at you, the leather holds and the chin behind it holds too.

talents.name: Top Billing
talents.desc: Your name above the title, in the biggest bulbs on the marquee. In a fight like this, everyone else is a supporting player.

talents.name: Second Wind
talents.desc: A gulp of air, a slap on the cheek, and the legs come back. Every stuntman knows the sweet moment just after the bell.

talents.name: Whetstone Habit
talents.desc: Between takes you sit on an apple box and stroke the blade across a stone. The prop men call it nerves. The blade calls it good.

talents.name: Switchblade Draw
talents.desc: Thumb on the button, blade out before the hand stops moving. Not one wasted motion between the pocket and the work.

talents.name: Cutting Room Floor
talents.desc: The editors at Paramount cut whole scenes in a breath. You've learned to cut just as fast, and leave as much on the floor.

talents.name: Sugar Glass
talents.desc: Prop bottles are boiled sugar and break pretty. Real ones break meaner, and there is always another one behind the bar.

talents.name: Union Break
talents.desc: Ten minutes every two hours, the contract says. You've learned to catch your breath in half that and still call it a break.

talents.name: Fairbanks Footwork
talents.desc: Douglas Fairbanks made swordplay look like dancing on his Santa Monica Boulevard lot. You picked up the footwork, and the knack for turning blades aside.

talents.name: Deep Pockets
talents.desc: A stuntman's coat has a pocket for everything: tape, smelling salts, a spare knife, a chocolate bar. You never run dry in a long fight.

talents.name: Thousand Cuts
talents.desc: No single cut finishes it. The hundredth does, or the thousandth, and you have nowhere else to be tonight.

talents.name: Fade Into Extras
talents.desc: In a borrowed coat a stuntman looks like forty other men in borrowed coats. The bugs strike at whoever moved last, and it wasn't him.

talents.name: Stand-In Steel
talents.desc: Stand-ins take the star's place under the hot lamps and the falling scenery. The work builds a forearm like a stevedore's.

talents.name: Cut to Ribbons
talents.desc: The cutting room never worked this fast. Blades flash left, right and left again until the chitin hangs off in strips.

talents.name: Scar Tissue
talents.desc: Every stuntman on Gower Street can read his career off his own hide. Old cuts heal tough, and tough is what pays the rent.

talents.name: Padded Costume
talents.desc: Wardrobe sews felt and horsehair under the cowboy shirt, where the camera can't see. It looks like nothing and stops plenty.

talents.name: Sandbag Landing
talents.desc: Down below, out of frame, somebody piled the sandbags right. A body that lands soft gets up again, and gets up mad.

talents.name: Clock Tower Nerve
talents.desc: Lloyd hung off a clock face above Broadway and smiled for the camera. After a few of those, a jump is just a jump.

talents.name: Featherweight Fall
talents.desc: Lean men fall cheap. He goes off the ledge like a dropped evening paper, loose and easy, saving his wind for the landing.

talents.name: Dive Roll
talents.desc: Hit the boards shoulder first, tuck, come up running. Done right, it costs a man no more than a good sneeze.

talents.name: Wire Walker
talents.desc: Piano wire strung between two catwalks, a balancing pole, and no net the insurance man would sign for. The feet learn fast.

talents.name: Safety Last
talents.desc: Somebody put it on a picture poster as a joke. Stuntmen took it as a working principle and learned to roll with the hit.

talents.name: Pratfall Timing
talents.desc: A banana peel is comedy; a banana peel at the right moment is art. The same beat puts a knife where the bug isn't guarding.

talents.name: Craft Services
talents.desc: Coffee in a tin cup and a ham sandwich off the lunch wagon. Strikes and invasions come and go, but the crew still eats.

talents.name: Box Office Draw
talents.desc: The crowd at Grauman's still cheers when a man falls off something tall. A stuntman fights better with an audience, even a frightened one.

talents.name: The Big Drop
talents.desc: The one they put on the poster: off the water tower, straight into the swarm. Nothing with six legs knows where he'll land.

talents.name: Ambulance Standing By
talents.desc: The studio keeps a Packard ambulance behind the set with the motor running. Knowing it's there makes a man last a little longer.

talents.name: Expert Badge
talents.desc: The Army pinned the Expert badge on men who stopped wasting breath on a shot. You still wear yours, inside the coat where it counts.

talents.name: Trench Patience
talents.desc: Months in a Flanders trench taught you to wait out anything. A dome of glass is only a longer wait.

talents.name: Sandbag Nest
talents.desc: A careful gunman never sets up anywhere he can't throw a few sandbags first. Burlap and sand stop more than people think.

talents.name: Iron Sights
talents.desc: No fancy glass on the barrel, just a notch and a post. Less to fuss with means less to fumble.

talents.name: Deep Breath
talents.desc: Fill the lungs, let half out, hold. Every rifleman learned it at camp, and it steadies more than the muzzle.

talents.name: Pinning Fire
talents.desc: Put rounds where the bug wants to go and it soon stops wanting to go anywhere. The legs are the easy part.

talents.name: Bolt-Action Rhythm
talents.desc: Lift, back, forward, down. The bolt finds its own tempo, like a fox-trot the band plays only for you.

talents.name: Snap Shooting
talents.desc: No time to shoulder it. Fire from wherever the gun already points and trust the years to do the aiming.

talents.name: Steady Under Fire
talents.desc: You learned in the Argonne that flinching never stopped a bullet. It turns out flinching doesn't stop acid either.

talents.name: Final Reel
talents.desc: Every picture saves its best shot for the last reel. So do you, and nobody walks out before the end.

talents.name: One Shot, One Bug
talents.desc: One cartridge, one carcass. The quartermaster at Post 43 counts every round of brass and likes your arithmetic.

talents.name: Sergeant York
talents.desc: York took 132 Germans in the Argonne with a rifle and a pistol. The bugs have never heard of him, but they will.

talents.name: Trick Holster
talents.desc: A cutaway holster bought off a Gower Gulch cowboy extra. The gun is out of the leather before the thought is finished.

talents.name: Matinee Idol
talents.desc: You watched Tom Mix do it a hundred Saturday afternoons. Somewhere along the way you started hitting what he only pretends to.

talents.name: Six-Gun Waltz
talents.desc: One-two-three, one-two-three, and the cylinder comes round again. The bugs never did learn to dance.

talents.name: Stunt Double
talents.desc: A stuntman on the Columbia lot taught you how to fall out of harm's way. Now and then you return the favour.

talents.name: Hot Lead
talents.desc: Fresh from the barrel and still smoking, it goes through chitin like a nail through a pine box.

talents.name: Rapid Reload
talents.desc: Six cartridges held between the fingers like a card sharp's deck. The cylinder is full before the empties hit the pavement.

talents.name: Wild West Show
talents.desc: Buffalo Bill's show folded years ago, but its sharpshooters drifted west to the pictures. You picked up their footwork and their swagger.

talents.name: Bullet Ballet
talents.desc: The dance directors at Fox would pay good money to film it: boots, smoke and gunfire, every step on the beat.

talents.name: Nickelodeon Nerves
talents.desc: You grew up in the front row of a nickel picture house, watching train robbers draw. Nothing on the Boulevard rattles a kid raised on that.

talents.name: Encore Shots
talents.desc: The crowd at a Wild West show always wanted one more. Fanning the hammer, you give the bugs their encore whether they asked or not.

talents.name: Ricochet Romance
talents.desc: Off a lamppost, off a fire hydrant, into the soft seam behind the carapace. Some shots you'd write home about, if the mail still ran.

talents.name: Extra Cylinders
talents.desc: A spare cylinder, already loaded, rides in the vest pocket. Swapping it takes a breath instead of a minute, and the mind stays on the work.

talents.name: Bug Spray
talents.desc: A Flit gun's worth of kerosene on the collar and cuffs. The small ones lose interest, and the big ones bite a little less sure.

talents.name: Game Warden
talents.desc: You walked the hills for the Fish and Game Commission before the Dome came down. Long miles of chaparral made you hard to wear out.

talents.name: Snare Line
talents.desc: Every trapper knows a crippled quarry is a caught one. You go for the legs quicker now, and the bugs offer plenty of legs to choose from.

talents.name: Scattergun
talents.desc: A double-barrel and a box of double-ought. You've learned to load by feel and fire without wasting a pellet's worth of thought.

talents.name: Thick Hide Coat
talents.desc: A steerhide coat off a Gower Gulch extra who won't be needing it. It turns a mandible about as well as it ever turned the rain.

talents.name: Big Game Nose
talents.desc: Out in Griffith Park you learned what a cornered animal smells like. The hive has a smell too, and it tells you where to aim.

talents.name: Exterminator's Pride
talents.desc: Before the Dome you rid bungalows of termites at two dollars a house. The pay is worse now, but the work has never felt better.

talents.name: Field Rations
talents.desc: A tin of corned beef, a canteen and a heel of bread, eaten crouched behind a billboard. A hunter learns to rest fast and rest anywhere.

talents.name: Bushwhacker
talents.desc: Lying in the sage above the Pass with your sights settled, you let the bug walk into the shot. Polite folks call it an ambush.

talents.name: Hard Country
talents.desc: Scrambling up the Hollywoodland slopes and down the dry washes every day keeps the legs quick and the hands quicker still.

talents.name: Swarm Season
talents.desc: When the hive spills out in autumn, nobody counts shells. The scattergun bucks and a whole knot of them comes apart at once.

talents.name: Old Trapper
talents.desc: Thirty winters in the Sierra taught you to step aside from a charging bear. A charging beetle is slower, and considerably uglier.

talents.name: Spark Gap
talents.desc: Set the electrodes a hair closer and the spark jumps on less juice. Every juicer on the Paramount lot learns it, or learns it the hard way.

talents.name: Live Rail
talents.desc: The Pacific Electric runs six hundred volts through its overhead wire. A smart electrician taps a little of it for himself and lets the railway pay.

talents.name: Crossed Wires
talents.desc: Two lines touch where they shouldn't, and the current goes looking for every bug in reach. Nobody calls it a mistake twice.

talents.name: Hollywood Current
talents.desc: The studios pull more power than half of Los Angeles. A man who has worked their switchboards learns to throw that weight around.

talents.name: Rubber Boots
talents.desc: Thick rubber soles, laced high. They won't stop a mandible, but they keep a fellow on his feet when the ground goes live.

talents.name: Quick Draw
talents.desc: Throw the switch before you've finished thinking about it. The bugs don't wait, and neither does a good juicer.

talents.name: Flash Point
talents.desc: Push the lines past their rating and everything nearby goes white for an instant. The smell of scorched chitin hangs around for days.

talents.name: Long Fuse
talents.desc: Ten years splicing cable teaches patience. The electrician who plans the whole circuit before laying a foot of it lives longest.

talents.name: Feedback Loop
talents.desc: The current runs out, comes round and runs back home. A man who wires himself into the loop gets back some of what he spent.

talents.name: Sparks Fly
talents.desc: When the arc catches just right it throws a fountain of sparks, the kind cameramen once paid good money to film.

talents.name: Bolt from the Blue
talents.desc: No warning, no thunder. One moment the bug is crossing Vine, the next it's a smoking shell and the streetlights are flickering.

talents.name: Shell Shock
talents.desc: Men who heard the guns at the Marne know the jolt of a near miss. A shock that floors a greenhorn barely rattles them.

talents.name: Klieg Eyes
talents.desc: Red, weeping, half blind from the lamps. Every old studio electrician has klieg eyes, and every one can aim a light without looking.

talents.name: Hot Spot
talents.desc: Every lamp has one place where the beam burns brightest. Put a bug's head there and watch it smoke.

talents.name: Barn Doors
talents.desc: Fold the hinged shutters in and the light pinches down to a blade. The short goes where it's sent and nowhere else.

talents.name: Footlights
talents.desc: The old vaudeville footlights warmed a stage from below. A little of that glow keeps an electrician's spirits up between fights.

talents.name: Gaffer Tape
talents.desc: A roll of black friction tape on the belt mends a bad splice in seconds. Gaffers swear by it; the bugs swear at it.

talents.name: Searchlight Sweep
talents.desc: Premiere-night searchlights still swing across the Dome, and the current follows the beam from one bug to the next.

talents.name: Sun Gun
talents.desc: A big arc lamp run hot enough to pass for noon. Location crews used them to fake daylight; now they cook bugs.

talents.name: Arc Lamp Glare
talents.desc: Throw the full glare in a bug's face and it can't tell where the light ends and the electrician begins.

talents.name: Gel Filter
talents.desc: A sheet of amber gelatin clipped over the lamp softens the glare. Somehow the bugs find you harder to pin down through it.

talents.name: Box Office
talents.desc: A full house means a full till. Every lamp you light seems to pay a little current back at the ticket window.

talents.name: Grand Premiere
talents.desc: Klieg lights sweep the sky like opening night for Hell's Angels at Grauman's, and every bug on the street is caught in the beam.

talents.name: Nitrate Stock
talents.desc: Old nitrate film burns hot, fast and mean, and no projectionist ever forgets it. Your live wire has picked up the same temper.

talents.name: Step-Up Coil
talents.desc: A wound transformer lifts the line voltage, and your spirits climb right along with it. Steady hands, steady current.

talents.name: Rubber Gloves
talents.desc: Thick black rubber, cracked at the knuckles, handed down from the man before you. Wrapping a pal in insulation comes cheaper with them on.

talents.name: Surge Protector
talents.desc: The breaker trips before the spike gets through, so the insulation is back on the line sooner than anybody expected.

talents.name: Power Station
talents.desc: You once stood inside an Edison substation at midnight and listened to it think. Some of that hum never left you.

talents.name: Carbon Brushes
talents.desc: Carbon brushes wear down so the dynamo doesn't. A good electrician learns to take the friction and keep turning.

talents.name: Heavy Load
talents.desc: Run every lamp on the stage off one circuit and the cable goes warm in your hands. Then the bugs find out why.

talents.name: Field Telephone
talents.desc: An olive-drab field telephone from the Argonne, rewired to ring the aid station. Help comes quicker when somebody bothered to string the line.

talents.name: Sandbagged
talents.desc: Grips weigh down light stands with sandbags so the wind can't topple them. Turns out the same trick works on electricians.

talents.name: Doughboy Ration
talents.desc: Corned willy and hardtack, the same tins the boys ate in France. Nobody likes it. Everybody stays on their feet.

talents.name: Dugout Shelter
talents.desc: Timber, sheet iron and a foot of packed earth. The men who dug in along the Marne taught the crews how to roof a generator pit.

talents.name: Powerhouse
talents.desc: The generator truck roars like a Southern Pacific locomotive, and the current you throw over a friend hums thick enough to stop a mandible cold.

talents.name: Ground Fault
talents.desc: Current always finds the shortest road to earth. You just make sure it runs through the bug on the way down.

talents.name: Nitrate Stock
talents.desc: Old nitrate film burns hotter than anything in the prop room. A few feet of last year's picture makes a cheaper flash than store-bought powder.

talents.name: Marshal's Blind Eye
talents.desc: A powder man breathes easier when the fire marshal is looking the other way, and a two-bit cigar keeps him looking.

talents.name: Cheap Fuse
talents.desc: Five-and-dime safety fuse from a hardware store on Cahuenga. It sputters and stinks, but it burns down just the same.

talents.name: Hot Klieg Lamps
talents.desc: Ten hours under the kliegs cooks a man's eyes and sharpens his wits. He learns what heat does to everything on a set.

talents.name: Quick Draw
talents.desc: A squib wired fast is a squib wired cheap. The old hands do it by feel between takes, a cigarette still lit.

talents.name: Fire Watch
talents.desc: Somebody has to stand by the bucket while the set burns. The fire watch learns to stand close and not flinch.

talents.name: Celluloid Blaze
talents.desc: Celluloid goes up like a grudge held too long: fast, hot and impossible to put out. A pinch of it goes into everything you light.

talents.name: Smouldering Reel
talents.desc: A reel left smouldering in its can is still burning when the projectionist comes back from lunch. So is whatever you lit.

talents.name: Asbestos Gloves
talents.desc: Stiff grey mitts that smell of a boiler room. They have saved more fingers on Poverty Row than any union rule.

talents.name: Burning Ambition
talents.desc: Every powder man dreams of the big one: the fall of Babylon, the Chicago fire. The dream keeps him reading chemistry books past midnight.

talents.name: Nitrate Inferno
talents.desc: When a nitrate vault goes, it goes all at once, and no fire company in Los Angeles can stop it. You have learned to start one on purpose.

talents.name: Final Reel
talents.desc: In the last reel, everything blows up. The audience expects it and the studio pays for it, so make the squibs count.

talents.name: Gas Mask
talents.desc: The same rubber mask that saw you through Ypres. It still smells of chlorine, and it still keeps you breathing inside your own smoke.

talents.name: Cheap Smoke
talents.desc: A smoke pot is tar paper, saltpetre and a coffee can. The studio pays for the real thing and never asks questions.

talents.name: Trench Coat
talents.desc: A khaki coat from the Somme, oiled and patched. It turned sleet in Flanders, and it turns a mandible well enough here.

talents.name: No Man's Land
talents.desc: Anyone who crossed no man's land learned to move low and fast through smoke. The legs remember even when the man would rather not.

talents.name: Smoke Signals
talents.desc: A few puffs in the right place tell the crew where you stand, and buy you a moment's rest behind the haze.

talents.name: Iron Lung
talents.desc: Years of breathing powder smoke on set have given you lungs like a Drinker respirator: tireless, wheezing and built of iron.

talents.name: Smoke and Mirrors
talents.desc: Half of Hollywood is smoke and the other half is mirrors. A tilted pane of glass doubles the cover for half the powder.

talents.name: Lingering Haze
talents.desc: Your smoke hangs over the set like morning fog off the ocean, and the bugs blunder about in it long after it should have cleared.

talents.name: Gas Drill
talents.desc: Eight seconds to get the mask on, the Army said. Powder men learned it twice: once in France, once beside the chlorine bottles on the effects stage.

talents.name: Cordite Haze
talents.desc: Through the drifting smoke of the last charge you can see where the bug's shell is thinnest. The bug cannot see you at all.

talents.name: Fog of War
talents.desc: In a good smoke screen a man is only a rumour. Claws snap shut on the spot where you were standing a moment ago.

talents.name: Studio Blackout
talents.desc: When the arcs go dark on the sound stage, the powder man is the only one who still knows exactly where every charge is buried.

talents.name: Blasting Cap
talents.desc: A copper tube no bigger than a cigarette, and the whole charge waits on it. Crimp it right and the bang comes clean.

talents.name: Bootleg Kegs
talents.desc: Cornero's boys left empty beer kegs all over the Valley. Packed with black powder, they hold a better load than they ever held beer.

talents.name: Sapper's Patience
talents.desc: The tunnellers at Ypres waited weeks in the clay, listening. Breathe slow, count the seconds, and let the fuse do the hurrying.

talents.name: Wrecking Crew
talents.desc: The studios tear down a set every Friday and build another by Monday. The powder man was always the fastest hand on a teardown.

talents.name: Hazard Pay
talents.desc: Union scale for handling explosives was a dollar more a day. The bugs pay nothing, but the hide you grew on the job still holds.

talents.name: Tamped Charge
talents.desc: Pack the hole with clay and tamp it hard. A tamped charge wastes nothing on noise and spends everything on the wall.

talents.name: Messines Ridge
talents.desc: June 1917: nineteen mines under the German line, and they heard it in London. A few of the men who dug them work in pictures now.

talents.name: Hard Hat
talents.desc: A tin hat from the Argonne, painted studio grey, dented by one falling klieg light and one very large mandible.

talents.name: Thick Skull
talents.desc: The effects foreman says you have been blown off your feet eleven times this year. You say nine. Neither of you remembers properly.

talents.name: Chain Reaction
talents.desc: Line the kegs up and light the first. The rest go off like a row of Keystone Cops tumbling down a staircase.

talents.name: The Big Bang
talents.desc: Every effects man dreams of the shot that needs no retake. The camera shakes, windows go out on Vine Street, and the hive comes down.

talents.name: Powder Monkey
talents.desc: The Navy's name for the boys who ran powder to the guns. You still run, crate on your shoulder, ducking under the falling sparks.

talents.name: Cheap Gauze
talents.desc: She buys gauze by the bolt from a Poverty Row wardrobe department and cuts it on her knee. It holds a wound as well as anything from Johns Hopkins.

talents.name: Cool Head
talents.desc: She has stood in a field hospital while the guns walked closer. A bug the size of a Ford sedan does not rattle her.

talents.name: Steady Hands
talents.desc: Her hands do not shake. Not for shellfire, not for ichor, not for a stuntman hollering about his collarbone.

talents.name: Cheap Ammonia
talents.desc: Household ammonia from the corner drugstore, decanted into little brown bottles. It wakes a man just as rudely as the expensive kind.

talents.name: Second Wind
talents.desc: Somewhere past the third casualty she stops feeling tired and simply keeps going, the way she did at Étaples in the spring of 1918.

talents.name: Hard Floor Sleeper
talents.desc: Ten minutes on bare linoleum between patients and she is up again. The Roosevelt Hotel's feather beds would only spoil her.

talents.name: Casualty Clearing Station
talents.desc: She sets up where the wounded fall: a tarpaulin, a lantern, two sawhorses and a door. It worked in Flanders and it works on Vine Street.

talents.name: Trench Constitution
talents.desc: Mud, lice, cold bully beef and trench fever. Anyone who came through all that is not about to be finished off by an insect.

talents.name: Brisk Rounds
talents.desc: Rubber soles squeak down the ward at a pace just shy of running. Head nurses have been timed against Charley Paddock and won.

talents.name: Stretcher Bearer
talents.desc: She learned more medicine carrying the stretcher than she ever did in lectures. You watch a man's face the whole way back.

talents.name: Angel of Mons
talents.desc: In 1914 the Tommies swore they saw angels over Mons. The boys she dragged off the Paramount lot swear they saw her.

talents.name: Clean Sheets
talents.desc: Boiled white, starched stiff, corners square enough to cut yourself on. Nothing creeps into a bed she has made.

talents.name: House Calls
talents.desc: She keeps a bicycle and a black bag by the door, and she knows which porch lights on Gower mean trouble.

talents.name: Cod Liver Oil
talents.desc: A spoonful every morning, whether you like it or not. Nobody likes it. It comes cheap by the case and lasts forever.

talents.name: Doctor's Orders
talents.desc: The doctor writes the order; she sees it carried out to the letter. Patients find it easier to argue with the bugs.

talents.name: Chloroform Calm
talents.desc: She moves through a fight like a ward at midnight, soft-footed and unhurried, and the hive's attention slides right past her.

talents.name: Sterile Field
talents.desc: Carbolic on every surface, instruments boiled, hands scrubbed to the elbow. Done properly, everything she touches goes exactly where she means it.

talents.name: Quiet Ward
talents.desc: Lights low, curtains drawn, a radio murmuring dance music at the far end. The patients mend faster, and so does she.

talents.name: Bedside Vigil
talents.desc: She sits up all night in a hard chair with her cap still pinned. Whatever comes for the patient has to come past her first.

talents.name: Laudanum Drip
talents.desc: A few drops in a glass of water, the old remedy. Not strictly legal, but nobody under the Dome is asking to see her license.

talents.name: Hospital Corners
talents.desc: Sheets folded tight, collar starched, cap pinned square. A nurse kept in that kind of order is a hard thing to knock over, and the bugs keep learning it.

talents.name: Penicillin Dream
talents.desc: A Scotsman in London found a mould that kills germs, the journals say. Nobody can bottle it yet, but she dresses every wound as if she could.

talents.name: Miracle of Lourdes
talents.desc: Pilgrims leave their crutches at the grotto. On the operating table she does not wait for the Virgin, though she would never refuse the help.

talents.name: Brisk Gait
talents.desc: Rubber heels on linoleum, never running, never late. A good ward nurse covers a city block between bells and arrives looking unhurried.

talents.name: Bunsen Burner
talents.desc: A steady blue flame under a flask of something nobody should drink. It heats slowly, it heats evenly, and it does not forgive.

talents.name: Volatile Mixture
talents.desc: Two clear liquids, one careless pour, and the beaker jumps off the bench. She has learned exactly how careless to be.

talents.name: Measured Drops
talents.desc: Ether by the drop, counted aloud, the way the old anaesthetists taught it. Nothing wasted, and every drop goes where it was meant to.

talents.name: Mustard Memory
talents.desc: She worked the gas wards at Étaples and still remembers the yellow blisters. The sedatives she mixes now carry a little of that remembering.

talents.name: Fume Hood
talents.desc: Behind the glass sash and the roaring fan, the vapours go up the flue instead of down her throat. She brought the habit out into the street.

talents.name: Cheap Reagents
talents.desc: Iodine by the gallon from a Glendale druggist who asks no questions. It stains the same brown and stings just as hard.

talents.name: Mad Scientist
talents.desc: She reads the German journals by lamplight and fills the margins with notes of her own. The orderlies have started knocking before they come in.

talents.name: Distillation
talents.desc: Copper tubing coiled in the back room, a slow drip into a clean jar. The revenue men assume bootlegging; she is only making things pure.

talents.name: Quiet Reagent
talents.desc: Colourless, odourless, slow to act. By the time the hive notices what she gave it, she is already across the room tending somebody else.

talents.name: Lethal Dosage
talents.desc: The same pharmacopoeia that tells her how to save a man lists, a page later, how much would kill one. She keeps that page dog-eared.

talents.name: Gas! Gas! Quick!
talents.desc: The shout every soldier knew from Flanders, the fumbling for masks, the green cloud rolling in low. Now it is the bugs who fumble.

talents.name: Rubber Gloves
talents.desc: Thick red rubber to the elbow, the kind the surgeons at County General swear by. Acid, ichor and broken glass all slide right off.

talents.name: Sawdust Trail
talents.desc: Every sinner who ever walked the sawdust trail to the mourner's bench left the preacher a little wiser about the human heart.

talents.name: Faith Healing
talents.desc: The pile of crutches by the platform tells the story. Call it the Lord or call it nerve, the cuts still close.

talents.name: Second Collection
talents.desc: When the plate comes back light, a seasoned preacher sends it round again and makes the hymn last on whatever the faithful can spare.

talents.name: Big Tent
talents.desc: Canvas big enough for the whole county, and room under it for every bruised soul who wanders in off the road.

talents.name: Radio Ministry
talents.desc: KFSG carries the Word clear across the Dome. A voice that steady is hard to shake, chittering hive or no.

talents.name: Circuit Rider
talents.desc: The old Methodist riders covered three counties on horseback. Their heirs cover Hollywood on foot, and nearly as quick.

talents.name: Hallelujah Moment
talents.desc: Sometimes the Spirit lands all at once, and the whole room shouts amen before the preacher has finished the sentence.

talents.name: Sunday Best
talents.desc: Pressed collar, shined shoes, hat brushed. A preacher who dresses the part spends less breath convincing the room.

talents.name: Soup Kitchen
talents.desc: With breadlines round the block, a preacher learns to make a little go a long way, whether it's soup or salvation.

talents.name: Altar Call
talents.desc: The organ swells, the lights come down, and the hurting come forward to the rail, where the preacher meets them with both hands.

talents.name: Angelus Temple
talents.desc: Five thousand seats and a radio tower in Echo Park. Something of that great white blaze travels with every preacher who ever sang there.

talents.name: Public Testimony
talents.desc: Stand before the congregation and tell what the Lord pulled you out of. After that, a bug bite seems a small thing.

talents.name: Soda Fountain
talents.desc: A cherry phosphate at the corner drugstore does everything a shot of rye once did, and the preacher is the first to say so.

talents.name: Sober Judgement
talents.desc: A clear-eyed man wastes nothing. He gives his blessing where it is needed and not a drop more.

talents.name: Volstead Act
talents.desc: The law of the land since 1920, and the preacher wears it like a breastplate, whatever the bootleggers think of it.

talents.name: Bone Dry
talents.desc: Not a drop since the Armistice. Twelve years of clean living builds a constitution the hive can't easily chew through.

talents.name: Clear Head
talents.desc: No Monday-morning fog, no shakes. The preacher reads the room and the Scripture sharper than any drinking man ever could.

talents.name: On the Wagon
talents.desc: Once you climb aboard the water wagon you learn to keep your balance, and to step lively when something lunges.

talents.name: Padlock Order
talents.desc: The dry agents chain a speakeasy shut in a minute flat. The preacher learns to slam the fear of God on a thing just as fast.

talents.name: Temperance Union
talents.desc: The ladies of the WCTU still meet Tuesdays, Dome or no Dome, and they send their preacher out with bandages rolled tight.

talents.name: Strict Abstinence
talents.desc: Not a drop since the Volstead Act, and the body thanks you for it. Insect venom finds a sober constitution a poor host.

talents.name: Carrie's Hatchet
talents.desc: Carrie Nation took a hatchet to every saloon bar in Kansas. Her heirs find a carapace splits as nicely as polished mahogany.

talents.name: Noble Experiment
talents.desc: Mr. Hoover called Prohibition a noble experiment. Whatever the bootleggers say, a blessing given bone-dry holds up well against claws.

talents.name: Pure Water
talents.desc: Hands scrubbed in clean Hollywood Reservoir water before they touch the wounded. Mr. Mulholland's water was always good for something.

talents.name: Pulpit Thumper
talents.desc: A man who pounds the lectern learns his scripture cold: chapter, verse, and the passages the bishop prefers to skip.

talents.name: Two-Bit Sermon
talents.desc: Short, cheap and to the point. The best street-corner preachers on Vine can damn a sinner before the red car passes.

talents.name: Wages of Sin
talents.desc: The wages of sin is death, says Romans. The hive has been running up a tab since the Dome came down.

talents.name: Fiery Tongue
talents.desc: The words come easier when you mean every one of them. A rebuke from the heart costs the preacher little and the bug plenty.

talents.name: Hard Pew
talents.desc: Forty years of Sunday mornings on unpadded oak build a constitution. Nothing the invaders spit compares to a three-hour August revival.

talents.name: Thunder Pulpit
talents.desc: Some voices need no radio station. This one rattles the stained glass in the back row and lifts the spirit with it.

talents.name: Old Testament
talents.desc: Leave the gentle parables for peacetime. Plagues, locusts and fire from heaven speak more plainly to things with six legs.

talents.name: Trench Faith
talents.desc: Plenty of men found God in a shell hole in the Argonne. He kept them breathing then, and some swear He's doing it again.

talents.name: Sulphur Ration
talents.desc: A little brimstone with the morning coffee, so to speak. The preacher's fire banks overnight and is roaring again by breakfast.

talents.name: Billy Sunday
talents.desc: Billy Sunday quit the Chicago White Stockings to slide into pulpits head-first. Preach his way and the rebuke lands like a fastball.

talents.name: Hellfire and Damnation
talents.desc: The full revival-tent treatment: sawdust trail, brimstone and a voice that cracks plaster. No bug comes forward to be saved.

talents.name: Slow Burn
talents.desc: A good sermon doesn't end at the amen. It smoulders under the shell for hours, like a cigarette tossed into dry hill brush.

talents.name: Fine Calibration
talents.desc: A turn of the jeweller's screwdriver and a squint through the loupe, and every contraption in the kit hits a hair closer to where it hurts.

talents.name: Thrown Spanner
talents.desc: A good mechanic never walks to fetch a wrench back. He throws it, and the hive learns to duck.

talents.name: Bootleg Current
talents.desc: Wire tapped straight off the Pacific Electric overhead. The welder runs hot and the power company never sends a bill.

talents.name: Tack Strip
talents.desc: Roofing tacks and carpet nails, swept into a coffee can and flung by the handful. Cheap as dirt and twice as mean.

talents.name: Union Battery
talents.desc: A wet-cell battery stamped with the IATSE local's number. Union-made, union-charged, and it keeps a man going well past quitting time.

talents.name: Patent Pending
talents.desc: The wrench has been filed, reshaped and improved past recognition. The Patent Office has three letters about it and has answered none.

talents.name: Short Circuit
talents.desc: Bare copper threaded through the tacks. A bug that steps down gets a nail in the foot and a jolt clean up the leg.

talents.name: Studio Roller Skates
talents.desc: Borrowed from the grips who use them to cross the big stages. Nobody looks dignified on them, but everybody arrives first.

talents.name: Edison's Spite
talents.desc: The Wizard of Menlo Park swore by perspiration. The mechanic adds one part plain meanness, and every blow lands sorer for it.

talents.name: Monkey Business
talents.desc: The monkey wrench comes round with a little extra English on it, the kind a man learns working nights on Poverty Row.

talents.name: Tesla's Revenge
talents.desc: The welder's arc jumps its gap and crawls up the bug like lightning down a church spire. Mr. Tesla would have enjoyed the show.

talents.name: Asbestos Gloves
talents.desc: Fireproof mitts from the effects shop, stiff as cardboard and thick as a porterhouse. A mantis claw finds precious little to bite.

talents.name: Shell Shock
talents.desc: A ringing blow to the carapace leaves the thing staggered and stupid, like a doughboy after a whizz-bang landed close.

talents.name: Lead Pipe
talents.desc: Plumber's lead pipe weighs more than it looks and asks less of the arm. The dime-novel detectives were right about it.

talents.name: Ten-Mile March
talents.desc: Camp Kearny taught him to walk ten miles under a full pack and complain the whole way. The legs remember, whether he likes it or not.

talents.name: Pick Handle Parry
talents.desc: An ash pick handle, held crosswise like a quarterstaff, turns aside a claw the same way it once turned aside a picket-line cop.

talents.name: Union Rates
talents.desc: The pile driver comes down for a fair day's wage and not a penny over. The local's business agent would approve.

talents.name: Coffee and Cigarettes
talents.desc: Black coffee from a thermos lid and a Lucky Strike behind the ear. The second wind comes quicker than any doctor would advise.

talents.name: Lights Out
talents.desc: Laid in just behind the antennae, the monkey wrench puts a bug to sleep quicker and cheaper than any bouncer on the Strip.

talents.name: Over the Top
talents.desc: When the whistle blew in France, a man climbed the ladder and ran. The legs and the nerve both came home with him.

talents.name: Brodie Helmet
talents.desc: A dented tin hat from the Argonne, bought for two bits off a Legion man. It rang like a church bell the first time a mandible found it.

talents.name: Iron Constitution
talents.desc: Twenty years of foundry smoke, bad coffee and worse landlords. A man built like that does not fold because a bug the size of a Ford leans on him.

talents.name: Demolition Man
talents.desc: Drive the pile hard and drive it true. The wreckers on Vine swear a good pile driver splits a hive wall like kindling.

talents.name: Sweatshop Pace
talents.desc: Ten-hour shifts on a rivet line teach a body to keep moving. Breaks are for the front office.

talents.name: Field Dressing
talents.desc: Clean rag, iodine and a strip of friction tape. Not pretty, but it holds until somebody with a proper bag comes along.

talents.name: Sandbag Walls
talents.desc: Sandbags stacked shoulder-high across Highland, the way the boys did it in France. Bugs chew through most things, but not burlap full of beach.

talents.name: Cheap Bandages
talents.desc: Torn bedsheets from the Roosevelt Hotel, boiled in a washtub out back. The management has not yet sent a bill.

talents.name: Foreman's Glare
talents.desc: The look that once kept a whole grip crew off the lunch wagon. It works on hive drones too, near enough.

talents.name: Sidestep Shuffle
talents.desc: Learned dodging swinging flats and runaway dollies on a soundstage floor. A pincer is slower than a falling sandbag, mostly.

talents.name: Quick Fix
talents.desc: Spit, wire and a sharp rap with the heel of the hand. Half the radios in Hollywood run on the same principle.

talents.name: Factory Recall
talents.desc: Every overhaul goes back to the book: original drawings, original tolerances. What the factory built, a careful man can build again.

talents.name: Lunch Pail
talents.desc: Two ham sandwiches, a boiled egg and coffee in the lid. Enough to carry a working man through a double shift on the barricades.

talents.name: Spit and Polish
talents.desc: A tidy bench and oiled tools keep a man's head clear. Wipe the wrench, wipe the brow, breathe.

talents.name: Warranty Work
talents.desc: Guaranteed for ninety days or ninety bugs, whichever comes first. The shop stands behind its work and does not charge twice.

talents.name: Good as New
talents.desc: When the job is done the plating sits flush and the man inside it stands straight. You would never know a bug had chewed either.

talents.name: Wrench Parry
talents.desc: A two-foot Stillson wrench turns a stinger as well as any cavalry sabre, and costs a good deal less.
